newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Sammi Steel sees net profit this year.
newsitem.headline: Sammi Steel sees net profit this year.

text.p: South Korea's largest stainless steel plate maker Sammi Steel Co sees its net account turning to profit this year from a huge loss in 1996, a company spokesman said on Saturday.
"We expect to post a 7.9 billion won profit this year by cutting back our debts," Hwang Chul-gyu told Reuters.
Last year, the company ran a net loss of 119.98 billion won, sharply up from a 39.45 billion won loss in 1995.
Hwang said the company's deal with Pohang Iron and Steel Co (POSCO) to sell most of its specialty iron rod production operations would help it repay snowballing debts.
Sammi is due to receive 719.4 billion won from POSCO under the deal, and Sammi plans to spend about 700 billion won of the total in repaying debts, Hwang said by telephone.
"The debt repayments will lead to a significant drop in our financial expenses this year," said Hwang.
The company's liabilities totalled 1.45 trillion won at the end of 1996, up from 1.31 trillion the year before.
Sammi's financial expenses incurred in connection with debts stood at 180 billion won in 1996 and Hwang predicted the figures would fall to as low as 40 billion won in 1997.
He also said its recent acquisition of quality assurance from Germany's TUV-Rhein Land on stainless steel plates would also help the company boost exports to the European Union.
Last year, Sammi's exports totalled 235.1 billion won, about a third of its total sales of 860.09 billion won.
Value of the company's exports to the European Union was not immediately available.
